new_task_1.title: Expose unpacked pytest marks through node.keywords on modules, classes, and functions
new_task_1.description: Pytest now records unpacked marks from `pytestmark`, function-level `pytestmark`, and parametrization marks directly in each collected node's `keywords` mapping, storing the actual `Mark` objects instead of placeholder boolean values. This makes marker-derived keyword lookups on `Module`, `Class`, and `Function` nodes consistent and preserves inherited visibility through `NodeKeywords` traversal.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that collected Python nodes expose unpacked marks consistently through their `keywords` mapping. Module-, class-, and function-level marks declared via `pytestmark` or attached directly to test callables must be inserted into `node.keywords` as their corresponding `Mark` objects, and function parametrization marks must also be reflected there. Marker inheritance should rely on normal parent traversal instead of flattening inherited markers into each node manually.

expectation.grounded: When `PyobjMixin.obj` unpacks marks from the underlying Python object, those marks must also be added to `self.keywords` as `(mark.name, mark)` pairs. During `Function` construction, `self.own_markers` must include unpacked function marks and any `callspec.marks`, then `self.keywords` must be populated in priority order from own markers, the function object's `__dict__`, and any explicit `keywords` argument. The implementation must no longer synthesize marker keywords as `True` values via `iter_markers()`.
expectation.conceptual: Marker names should appear in `node.keywords` with their real mark payloads, not just as truthy sentinels. Consumers inspecting collected nodes should see the same marker object at the level where it is declared, while inherited marker visibility should come from parent keyword lookup semantics.

constraints.grounded: Existing non-marker keyword entries from the function object's `__dict__` and explicit constructor `keywords` must still work and retain higher priority where they use the same key. Parent traversal behavior in `NodeKeywords` must remain responsible for inherited visibility, so function nodes should only write their own markers locally. Yield-test collection behavior and other collection paths must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must improve marker visibility without regressing keyword deduplication or overriding unrelated custom keywords. Plugins and internal code that read `item.keywords['marker_name']` should receive stable, meaningful values across module, class, and function collectors.

behavior: A module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.foo` causes `module.keywords['foo']` to contain the `foo` mark object.
A class-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.bar` causes `class.keywords['bar']` to contain the `bar` mark object while leaving the enclosing module without a `bar` entry.
A function-level mark such as `test_method.pytestmark = pytest.mark.baz` causes `function.keywords['baz']` to contain the `baz` mark object without adding `baz` to ancestor nodes.

A function node can resolve inherited module/class marks through keyword lookup traversal, so `function.keywords['foo']` and `function.keywords['bar']` are available even when only declared on ancestors.
Parametrization-applied marks stored in `callspec.marks` are added to the function node's own markers and keyword mapping as mark objects.
Marker keyword entries are no longer stored as bare `True` placeholders when a real `Mark` object is available.
acceptance_criteria: Given a module marked with `pytest.mark.foo`, a class marked with `pytest.mark.bar`, and a method marked with `pytest.mark.baz`, the collected function node exposes `foo`, `bar`, and `baz` in `item.keywords` as mark objects.
In the same scenario, the class node exposes `foo` and `bar` as mark objects but does not expose `baz`.
In the same scenario, the module node exposes `foo` as a mark object and does not expose `bar` or `baz`.
If a function has parametrization marks, those marks are present in the function node's keyword mapping as mark objects.
If a custom keyword or object attribute uses the same key as a marker, the documented constructor and object-attribute priority order is preserved.

new_task_2.title: Raise ImportPathMismatchError when import_path loads a module without __file__
new_task_2.description: The `import_path` helper now treats imported modules with `__file__ is None` as an import-path mismatch and raises `ImportPathMismatchError` explicitly instead of continuing into filename normalization logic. This gives callers a stable pytest-specific failure mode for namespace-package or directory imports that do not resolve to a concrete file.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `_pytest.pathlib.import_path` handles imported modules whose `__file__` attribute is `None` by raising `ImportPathMismatchError` immediately. The function must not attempt to call path normalization methods such as `endswith()` on a `None` value, and it must report the mismatch using pytest's existing import-mismatch error type.

expectation.grounded: Inside `import_path`, after importing the module and before normalizing `.pyc`, `.pyo`, or `__init__.py` suffixes, the code must check `mod.__file__`. If it is `None`, raise `ImportPathMismatchError(module_name, module_file, path)`. The existing `PY_IGNORE_IMPORTMISMATCH=1` bypass must remain intact.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest imports a path but ends up with a module object that has no backing file, it should fail in a predictable pytest-specific way rather than crashing with a generic attribute error or producing an unclear mismatch state.

constraints.grounded: The new check must only affect the normal mismatch-validation path when `PY_IGNORE_IMPORTMISMATCH` is not set to `1`. Modules with a valid `__file__` must continue through the existing normalization and same-file comparison logic unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The change should improve error reporting for edge cases without altering successful imports or the existing opt-out behavior for mismatch checks.

behavior: If `import_path` imports a module whose `__file__` is `None`, it raises `ImportPathMismatchError` immediately.
If the imported module has a normal file path, mismatch detection still strips `.pyc` or `.pyo` suffixes and handles `__init__.py` paths as before.
If `PY_IGNORE_IMPORTMISMATCH=1` is set, the mismatch check continues to be skipped.
acceptance_criteria: Calling `import_path` on a path that resolves to a module object with `__file__ is None` raises `ImportPathMismatchError` instead of failing with an unrelated exception.
Calling `import_path` on a normal module file continues to succeed exactly as before.
Calling `import_path` with `PY_IGNORE_IMPORTMISMATCH=1` still bypasses mismatch validation, including the new `__file__ is None` guard.
